Since robots are unable to dream, humans have started making dream machines to solve this problem and help them out. Thanks to your own workshop, take part in the amazing MECH A DREAM project over the course of the week you have been allotted: make the most dreams for your robot by optimizing your resources and the construction time of your machines. At last, your mechanical friend will be able to answer the age-old question: Do androids dream of electric sheep? Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview & Round Summary 2 Day Turns 3 Work in Factory 4 Delivery Dock (Delivery) 5 Stock Room (Production) 6 Work in Workshop 7 Machines Overview and Buying Machines 7.1 Aspects of a Machine 7.2 To Buy a Machine 8 Build Machines 9 Night 10 End Game Triggers 11 Final Scoring Overview & Round Summary This game takes place over 7 days (rounds). This is tracked at the bottom of the Shared Board. Each day consists of 4 turns: Morning (Green zone, Rising Sun), Afternoon (Blue/Teal zone, Full Sun), Evening (Orange zone, Setting Sun), and Night (Purple Power Button). Day Turns Each Day turn has two Major Choices: The Factory, or the Workshop. These Major Choices both have two choices; resulting in four actions to choose from per turn. Work in Factory The Factory is the bottom half of the Shared Board. The "Delivery Dock" (Delivery) on the bottom left, and "Stock Room" (Production) on the bottom right. Delivery Dock (Delivery) Pay the Flowers cost at the top of the bar to gain the rewards for the Time of Day. Morning gives more rewards than Afternoon and Evening. Afternoon gives more than Evening. "Purple squares with a gear"-rewards, allow you to activate a completed machine. Stock Room (Production) Gain 6, 4, or 2 resources favoring either more Flowers or more Ink. Visiting earlier in the day gains you more resources. Morning: 2 Flowers & 4 Ink OR 4 Flowers & 2 Ink. Afternoon: 1 Flowers & 3 Ink OR 3 Flowers & 1 Ink. Evening: 2 Flowers OR 2 Ink. The maximum amount of Flowers or Ink you can store is 9, this is tracked on the Bottom Left and Bottom Right of your personal board. Work in Workshop The Workshop is the top half of the Shared Board where you can Buy Machines (marketplace), and the top half of your personal board where you can Build Machines (conveyor belt). Machines Overview and Buying Machines Aspects of a Machine Left side shows Cost in Ink, Right side shows Time it takes to Build. Middle shows what you can do once built: Input in upper left (There may be no input cost), to Output in bottom right (Flowers, Ink, Rainbows, Time, Sheep/VP.) Green machines are special permanent effects, mind the tooltip! To Buy a Machine Choose one from the marketplace, pay the cost in Ink, place a Worker on it, and put it on your conveyor belt where the Timer indicates. Multiple Machines may occupy the same space on your conveyor belt, but only machines with a worker may move. Build Machines Place a Worker on a Machine on your conveyor belt to boost its movement. At the end of each Turn (Morning, Afternoon, Evening), machines move forward equal to the number of workers on them: i.e. 1 time space with 1 worker, 2 time spaces with 2 workers, etc. When a machine leaves your conveyor belt, it is completed. It will flip from the building side, to the completed side, and sit in the center of your personal board. Night First, All workers return to their spaces on your personal board. You may activate all completed, purple, machines as you wish, or are able, in the order of your choosing. These sit in the center of your personal board. This includes your "Default Machine", which sits above your completed machines zone, and below space 2 & 3 of your conveyor belt. This grants you 1 Ink in the base game. Any benefits which cause in progress machines to be completed, will then give the player the immediate bonus of completing that machine After the end of Night check

[Rating: 5/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  I'd play again but it is nothing I need to own. Three shifts where you take an action building a dream engine. The night shift is the most fun where you get to operate all your built machines.

[Rating: 5/10] It's fine for a worker placement game with a conveyor:)  It didn't really do anything to stand out from other euros in my one play.  I'd play again. Choosing to use workers to boost movement of a factory tile or to get stuff can be interesting.

[Rating: 5/10] Decently fine worker placement efficiency and timing puzzle, but it was too much of a solitaire game for me. So many shared worker placement spaces mean and personal board stuff means that the tightness and interaction of typical worker placement design is not present. Love the art style, but not sure how much it helps for ease of understanding during the game.

[Rating: 5/10] A very basic worker placement game, other than claiming the tiles there is no competition for spots at all.  Furthermore, the point progression on the machines often do not make sense.  One rainbow can convert to 3 dream points but two is worth less at 5?  One water or one flower is worth 2 each but for both is only 3?  Machines that require more resources somehow covert into less points, which honestly made me felt robbed instead of accomplished round after round.  Mech A Dream just didn’t do much for me and I would not recommend it.

[Rating: 5/10] --Jan2024-- Perhaps less compelling when one's left neighbour keep taking the machines one wanted, and the thing that replaces it is less interesting.  That aside, I also fought initially with the representation: I didn't know what much of the game state meant.  In the end, the game wasn't terrible; but I'm in no hurry to reprise it.

Resources and visuals are very thematic and interesting but the mechanics don't make me feel like I am creating dreams.
